➡️ Stronger focus on career pathways (not just subjects)

The Literacy and Numeracy for Adults Assessment Tool (LNAAT) is an online adaptive assessment designed to provide robust and reliable information about the reading, writing, numeracy and vocabulary skills of adults.
 
Used widely across New Zealand’s tertiary education system, the LNAAT helps educators and organisations better understand capability, inform targeted support and track progress over time.
 
Previously managed by the New Zealand Council for Educational Research (NZCER), we have transitioned the LNAAT continuity of service, strengthens system-wide capability and aligns the LNAAT more closely with TEC’s wider literacy and numeracy stewardship role.
 
The knowledge base brings together guidance, resources and support materials in one place, making it easier for educators, providers and organisations to effectively use the tool. It provides clear, accessible information on how to administer assessments, interpret results and support people to build their literacy and numeracy skills.

1️⃣ Using Tahatū in career planning

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="feed-reshare-content__commentary">For our second volunteer role model feature this National Volunteer Week, we have kickass lawyer <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/salavalasi-su-a-79990892?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Salavalasi Su'a</a>. 😎

What does it take to build a career guided by purpose and values? ⚖️

Salavalasi Sua’s journey into law is grounded in her culture, faith and a strong commitment to fairness and justice.

Her greatest joy is helping people access justice and being a voice for them through some of the most challenging times in their lives. 

Salavalasi faced her own challenges being a Pacific Island woman and a minority in the legal profession, which fuelled her success.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Expanded <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/inspiring-the-future-aotearoa?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Inspiring the Future Aotearoa</a> event formats support senior student pathways

We’ve added three new event formats designed to better support senior secondary students who are ready for more focused, meaningful career interactions. 

While our original formats help to broaden horizons, these new options go further - supporting students to explore real career pathways, tertiary study and next steps beyond school. 

➡️ Stronger focus on career pathways (not just subjects) 
➡️ Designed for Year 11+ and advanced learning 
➡️ Aligned to curriculum and NCEA Levels 2 & 3 
➡️ Flexible, easy-to-run formats 

👉 New formats at a glance 

1️⃣ Career Chat – ideal for smaller groups; hear from one or more role models 
2️⃣ Career Discussion Group – groups have deeper conversations with role models (Year 11+) 
3️⃣ Role model Interview – highly interactive, student-led conversations (Year 11+) 

These formats help students move from inspiration to action with a clear pathway forward - especially when paired with Tahatū Career Navigator. 

👉 Explore the new formats and plan or book an event for Term 3 or 4: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/ebHMN9Ya?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/ebHMN9Ya</a>

Let’s make career learning more relevant, focused and impactful.</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">You can now access the LNAAT knowledge base on the TEC website
 
The Literacy and Numeracy for Adults Assessment Tool (LNAAT) is an online adaptive assessment designed to provide robust and reliable information about the reading, writing, numeracy and vocabulary skills of adults.
 
Used widely across New Zealand’s tertiary education system, the LNAAT helps educators and organisations better understand capability, inform targeted support and track progress over time.
 
Previously managed by the New Zealand Council for Educational Research (NZCER), we have transitioned the LNAAT continuity of service, strengthens system-wide capability and aligns the LNAAT more closely with TEC’s wider literacy and numeracy stewardship role.
 
The knowledge base brings together guidance, resources and support materials in one place, making it easier for educators, providers and organisations to effectively use the tool. It provides clear, accessible information on how to administer assessments, interpret results and support people to build their literacy and numeracy skills.
